comparisons.interpretation: Leuba emphasizes obtaining withheld records for public requesters; O'Connor emphasizes dashboards, searchable contracts and budget disclosure. These transparency mechanisms can complement one another.
Leuba would use his seat to ask excluded public questions; O'Connor seeks more state-granted authority for the board. Both identify accountability problems, using different proposed routes.
Both call attention to inadequate county staffing and the need to strengthen service capacity, rather than treating every fiscal-watchdog candidate as favoring staff cuts.

Leuba emphasizes donor independence and public legal challenges; O'Connor emphasizes his voting record and ethics proposals. Neither candidate's assertions about independence are independently certified by this comparison.

Shrestha presents the district as a leader in statewide change; Madden emphasizes hands-on local responsiveness and service delivery. The difference is stated emphasis, not proof that either rejects the other's goals.

Shrestha questions corporate contributions when public financing is available; Madden rejects treating contributions as proof of policy commitments. Their campaign-finance arguments do not substitute for direct evidence of specific policy positions.

Green emphasizes public ownership and rejects privatizing public goods; Blackwell is open to private infrastructure and partnerships subject to public input and inclusion requirements. This describes their stated delivery strategies.
Both explicitly support a Pennsylvania Green New Deal, although their detailed programs and financing emphases are not identical.

Green marks yes and Blackwell marks no on the same question about a moratorium on all new charter schools. The unelaborated Blackwell response is not generalized into support for every form of school privatization.
Both mark support for state single payer covering residents regardless of documentation status. Their differences on other issues do not erase this agreement.

Green marks support for ending the death penalty in all cases; Blackwell marks opposition to that universal abolition proposition. No specific exception or sentencing policy is invented for Blackwell.

Green emphasizes progressive legislative and movement coalitions; Blackwell emphasizes bipartisan agreement around nonprofit delivery and measurable results. Both describe coalition work rather than categorical refusal to cooperate.
